items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: Michael Levy was the teacher in the Williamsville School District.

ctx.x: Have you noticed a difference in working with the sidemen people, sidewomen people, working with schooled musicians and people who are mostly self-taught, how they absorb the music, how they memorize it, how they learn it?

Almost everybody out there is a combination. I am. I had piano lessons when I was a little kid and then in high school I started teaching myself. My music teacher would say, as I wanted to get better, he said, “well try the Bach two part inventions.” So I learned all © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -19-

those, and then he gave me “The Well Tempered Clavier,” and then I remember Emerson, Lake and Palmer came out with “Pictures at an Exhibition,” and it had probably been out for a while but, you know, it was a record club thing. I think I bought “Tarkus” was their first record, because it had a little giant armadillo on it and I thought, oh that’s a cool cover.
